global_caption: The video contains 15 shots and is a realistic cool-toned piano tutorial. The overall color palette is dominated by cool gray-blue tones, with lighting primarily from overcast natural light near the window and soft overhead indoor lighting. Camera movement is controlled and stable, prioritizing clarity for instructional purposes. The emotional tone remains consistently calm and focused.
shot1: Shot 1 opens directly with a wide eye-level composition, placing the electronic keyboard and a young woman seated before it along the center axis of the frame. The foreground includes the edge of the bench, while the background reveals a rain-wet window and softly blurred classroom walls. Shallow depth of field keeps the subject and instrument in focus. Cool natural light from the side-rear outlines her silhouette. She sits upright, shoulders relaxed, right hand hovering above the keys ready to demonstrate.
shot2: Shot 2 cuts hard from the previous shot, featuring a close-up eye-level view centered on the central area of the keyboard. Black and white keys form horizontal leading lines, with focus locked near middle C. The sleeve and body of the piano in the background are blurred. Soft cool lighting continues.
shot3: Shot 3 cuts hard from the previous shot, showing an overhead close-up from directly above the right hand and central key area. The back of the hand, fingertips, and adjacent black keys are clearly visible. Composition places middle C slightly below center. Diffused cool light from the window evenly illuminates the scene. Finger 1 accurately presses down on middle C, fingertip naturally curved, knuckles stable. The small displacement of the key depression is clearly visible, accompanied by a crisp single key press The camera remains static to emphasize teaching accuracy.
shot4: Shot 4 cuts hard from the previous shot with action matching, shifting to a close-up eye-level view from the front side of the keyboard. The foreground shows the already released middle C, focus shifts to the D key. Under the same cool soft lighting, finger 2 drops from above onto D, palm maintains natural arch, wrist not overly raised. Key press The camera slightly pushes in to highlight the position of finger 2 pressing the key.
shot5: Shot 5 cuts hard from the previous shot, continuing the close-up eye-level view with a slight pan to the right along the keyboard. The group of black keys forms a rhythmic background reference, focus lands on the E key and fingertip of finger 3. The young woman uses finger 3 to press E, pad contact stable, first two fingers naturally retracted without tension. The full process of the key cap sinking is fully presented. The camera performs a very short distance follow pan to complete the key press display.
shot6: Shot 6 cuts hard from the previous shot, showing a medium close-up from a slightly forward overhead angle. The frame simultaneously includes the thumb, palm, and transitional space before the F key. The composition shifts focus from individual keys to hand structure. Under cool lighting, the relaxed palm and rounded back of the fingers are clearly visible. The young woman slowly demonstrates the key action of the thumb passing under the palm. After finger 3 completes its previous position and lifts to form a channel, the thumb smoothly slides into the new landing preparation area. The motion is continuous and not stiff. The camera makes slight tilt adjustments to follow, emphasizing the core difficulty in the tutorial.
shot7: Shot 7 cuts hard from the previous shot with continuous action, showing an overhead close-up directly facing the F key area, focus concentrated on the position of finger 1 after completing the crossover. Lighting remains consistent. Finger 1 follows through to press F, thumb joint does not collapse, wrist still maintains a steady arc. Single key press The camera remains stable, allowing viewers to clearly see the correct result after the crossover.
shot8: Shot 8 cuts hard from the previous shot, showing a close-up eye-level view with a slight side angle. Composition places the G key at the golden ratio point of the frame. Slight cold reflection appears on the foreground key surface. Finger 2 sequentially presses G, other fingers naturally hover. Motion is concise and accurate. The camera makes a minor push-in to reinforce the sense of step-by-step progression.
shot9: Shot 9 cuts hard from the previous shot, continuing the close-up eye-level view moving further right along the keyboard, focus shifting to the A key. Finger 3 drops to press A, relationship between key press and finger number is clear. Fingertip remains rounded and properly weighted.
shot10: Shot 10 cuts hard from the previous shot, showing a close-up eye-level view closer to the higher register, with B key and finger 4 as absolute visual centers. Background high-register keys gradually blur to create depth. When finger 4 presses B, the back of the hand remains smooth without outward flipping. Changes in hand shape and key press are clearly visible under mixed cool top-side soft lighting. The camera makes a brief push-in then stops.
shot11: Shot 11 cuts hard from the previous shot, showing a close-up overhead view locked on high C. Adjacent black keys in the foreground provide clear positioning reference. Shallow depth of field makes the fingertip of finger 5 sharpest. Finger 5 firmly presses high C, completing the ascending endpoint. Fingertip support is clear, palm arch complete. The note onset is perfectly synchronized with the image. The camera gently lifts slightly, visually concluding the ascent.
shot12: Shot 12 transitions from the previous shot with a fade-in continuation of motion, showing a medium close-up eye-level view displaying a segment of keyboard from central to high register and the entire right hand. Composition is wider, allowing both hand shape and scale path to be seen. Soft reflections from cool rainy-day lighting appear on the key surfaces. The young woman slowly and continuously plays the ascending C major scale. Fingers move sequentially, thumb crossover smooth, wrist gently follows without excessive movement. Continuous piano The camera performs a smooth lateral follow pan, synchronizing scale flow with image movement.
shot13: Shot 13 cuts hard from the previous shot, showing an overhead medium close-up from directly above recording the descending return path. The entire route from high C back to central area is clearly readable. She begins from high C and descends in correct order back to central area. Wrist remains stable without collapsing. Continuous descending notes perfectly correspond to finger movements. The camera makes a slight leftward pan to follow the return path, completing the closed-loop step.
shot14: Shot 14 cuts hard from the previous shot, returning to a medium eye-level view of the subject and piano from one side. The frame includes forearm, wrist, and half-body sitting posture. Background rain-streaked window and classroom remain consistent. Focus is on the contour of the right wrist.
shot15: Shot 15 concludes with a natural hard cut from the previous shot, returning to a wide eye-level view that re-establishes the full teaching space. The electronic keyboard, sitting posture, rain outside the window, and cool-toned classroom are all included in the frame. Foreground-background relationships remain stable, with the person and instrument again centered to create a bookend effect. She ends in the standard hand position, wrist slightly arched, fingers rounded and hovering above the keys. The camera slowly pulls back to complete a calm, professional instructional conclusion.
